newsitem.title: UK: N Sea crudes look set for further move down.
newsitem.headline: N Sea crudes look set for further move down.

text.p: Barrels of North Sea crudes looked set to sell at cheaper prices on Monday as refiners' margins continued weak and supply outstripped demand for March-loading crude oil, traders said.

Brent fell sharply -- both on an outright basis and for physical barrels against April. Three March cargoes were heard traded at April Brent -35 cents, down from April -24 cents for a March 18-20 cargo on Friday.
A March 21-23 Ekofisk moved at Dated Brent +20 cents. With up to five further cargoes remaining unsold in March many expected the next traded level to be lower.
One refiner was heard reoffering two end month cargoes and picking up cheaper West African barrels.
"This (North Sea crude) market is a dog - and a sick one," one equity holder said.
Up to three Oseberg cargoes were also heard to have moved but details were not forthcoming and traders saw differentials there falling sharply as well.

Three March 25-27 Brent cargoes turned wet on Monday. These included two deferrals following Friday's five o' clockings. Two cargoes were kept by Arcadia and Koch was heard five o' clocked with the third.
The Brent April/May spread was actively traded up from early deals at +15 cents to a high of +18 cents but by late talk bids were as low as +12 cents.
"It's all falling apart. The margins are horrible and people just don't need to buy crude. Some barrels are going to trade at very low prices but the deals will never be confirmed," one refiner said.
Apart from Forties just about every other sweet North Sea crude still had unsold March barrels.
On CFD's, this week traded earlier at April -35 cents but buying died off as outright levels lost ground.
